brief:
# Seagrape Family Dental: research brief

_Sample report. Seagrape Family Dental is a fictional practice created to preview this tool. Competitors are described by type with names and URLs withheld, and no reviews or ratings were collected._

## 1. What the business does and for whom

Seagrape Family Dental is a family and cosmetic dental practice in Coconut Grove, Miami. Two dentists, Dr. Elena Ruiz, DMD, and Dr. Andrés Molina, DDS, treat children and adults. The homepage lists six services: cleanings and exams, pediatric dentistry, Invisalign, teeth whitening, dental implants and emergency dentistry. The footer gives office hours as Monday to Saturday, and the contact page says emergency patients can be seen the same day.

The team is bilingual. The homepage says: “About half of our patients prefer to speak Spanish, and our whole team speaks English and Spanish.” The practice’s natural audience is local families, many of them Spanish-speaking, plus adults interested in cosmetic work and anyone with a toothache who needs to be seen today.

## 2. Brand and positioning

The current voice is friendly but generic. Lines like “Your Smile Is Our Priority” and “Gentle Care For The Whole Family” could belong to any practice. The real strengths are buried or missing:

- **Language.** A fully bilingual team is a genuine advantage, yet the homepage says so once, as “Se Habla Español” in the footer.
- **Same-day emergencies.** On the homepage this is just “Emergency Dentistry” in a list of services.
- **Saturdays.** Hours appear only in the footer.
- **One practice for the whole family.** Kids’ checkups and cosmetic work under one roof means one dentist for parents and children.
- **The name.** Sea grape trees line Miami’s shoreline. “Seagrape” is local, memorable and visual, and the current site does nothing with it.

## 3. Competitors

Because this is a sample, competitors are described by type rather than named.

- **Large dental chains in Brickell** (names withheld in this sample). Sites in this group are built around booking, with a Book button on every page and online scheduling. They read as corporate, and Spanish is usually limited to a language toggle on the booking step.
- **Two independent practices on Coral Way** (names withheld in this sample). Both have newer sites with tap-to-call phone numbers and Spanish versions of their main pages. One shows its dentists on the homepage. Neither offers online booking.
- **Pediatric-only practices in Coral Gables** (names withheld in this sample). Bright, playful sites aimed at parents. They compete for kids’ visits but don’t treat adults, which leaves room for a practice that cares for the whole family.

Of the sites reviewed, Seagrape’s is the only one with neither a tappable phone number nor online booking.

## 4. What customers look for and search for

People choosing a dentist want quick answers: is it close, do they handle what I need, can I get in soon, and will someone speak my language. Their searches follow the same lines:

- **Place:** “dentist Coconut Grove”, “family dentist near me”
- **Language:** “dentista en Coconut Grove”, “dentista que habla español Miami”
- **Urgency:** “emergency dentist Miami”, “same day dentist near me”
- **Treatment:** “Invisalign Coconut Grove”, “teeth whitening Miami”, “dental implants Miami”
- **Children:** “pediatric dentist Coconut Grove”, “kids dentist near me”
- **Schedule:** “dentist open Saturday Miami”

The current site has no page built for any one of these searches, and Spanish searches have nothing to land on.

## 5. Problems with the current website

**Speed.** Google Lighthouse (mobile) scores performance 34/100. The largest element appears after 6.8 s and the first content after 3.1 s. Speed Index is 7.4 s, Total Blocking Time is 1,240 ms and layout shift is 0.31. Google’s Core Web Vitals guidance (web.dev) counts an LCP under 2.5 s and a CLS under 0.1 as good. The server took 1.9 s to respond, and the homepage HTML alone is 240 KB, loading 24 scripts and 14 stylesheets (measured).

**Conversion.** There is no online booking. The only form on the homepage is the site search (measured: 1 form). The phone number, (305) 555-0187, is part of an image in the header, so it can’t be tapped, copied or read by a screen reader. Our scan found no phone number in the homepage text; the number appears as text only on the contact page.

**Language.** No Spanish pages and no hreflang tags (measured). Apart from “Se Habla Español”, the homepage is English only.

**SEO.** The title tag is “Home” (4 characters). There is no meta description, no H1, no structured data and no Open Graph tags (measured). The sitemap lists 9 URLs, none of them for a single service.

**Design and content.** The hero is an auto-rotating slider of stock photos (the image files are named “shutterstock_…”). The “Latest News” block shows posts from 2017 and 2016, the footer reads “© 2016”, and the generator tag reports WordPress 4.5.3, a 2016 release.

**Accessibility.** Lighthouse scores accessibility 71/100, and 22 of 31 images have no alt text (measured). The theme stylesheet sets body text at 13px and captions in light gray (#999999) on white, about 2.8:1 contrast, below the 4.5:1 WCAG AA minimum for body text.

## 6. Opportunities

- **Lead with Spanish.** A complete Spanish site, written by a fluent writer rather than machine-translated, answers searches that currently find nothing and speaks to the half of patients who, by the practice’s own count, prefer Spanish.
- **Make booking the main action.** Online booking and a tappable number on every page, with a separate fast path for emergencies.
- **Own local searches.** A page per service in both languages, Dentist schema, a real title and a Google Business Profile that matches the site.
- **Use the name.** “Seagrape” gives the brand a ready-made visual world: round leaves, coastal light, local roots.
- **Make speed part of the first impression.** A lean rebuild can bring mobile loading inside Google’s “good” range.

summary.headline: New patients can’t book online, tap to call, or read it in Spanish.
paragraphs: Seagrape Family Dental already offers what Coconut Grove families look for: two dentists who see kids and adults, a team that speaks English and Spanish, same-day emergency visits and Saturday hours. The website shows none of that in the first few seconds. Visitors get a rotating stock-photo slider, a page titled “Home” and no headline.

Taking the next step is hard, too. There is no online booking, and the phone number is an image, so it can’t be tapped on a phone. Google Lighthouse scores mobile performance 34 out of 100, and the main content takes 6.8 seconds to appear. The site itself says about half of patients prefer Spanish, yet there isn’t a single Spanish page.

The rebuild should do four things: load fast on phones, let patients book online or call with one tap, offer every page in English and Spanish, and tell Google clearly what the practice is and where. All three design directions below do that. They differ in look and feeling: calm and clear, warm and illustrated, or bold and bilingual.

keyNumbers.label: Until the main content appears on a phone (Largest Contentful Paint)
Homepage images with no alt text
Spanish pages declared to search engines (hreflang tags)

firstSeconds.observation: The screen is still white. On a phone, the first content takes 3.1 seconds to appear (Google Lighthouse, mobile), so the very first impression is a wait, not a welcoming practice.
Still blank. Nothing yet says dentist, Coconut Grove or Spanish, and a visitor who arrived from a search result can tap Back at no cost.
The header and the first slide begin to paint: a stock photo captioned “Welcome to Seagrape Family Dental” in small type. The page jumps as the slider loads (layout shift 0.31, Google Lighthouse).

The main slide has finally loaded (LCP 6.8 s), but the visitor still can’t see the services, the Spanish-speaking team or the Saturday hours. There is no Book button, and tapping the phone number does nothing because it is an image.

findings.title: There is no way to book online
findings.evidence: The homepage has one form, and it is the site search (measured: 1 form). The navigation offers “Contact Us” and “Patient Forms” but no booking link. The only way to make an appointment is to call.
findings.impact: Anyone looking for a dentist in the evening or on a Sunday, when the office is closed, can’t take the next step. They may book with a practice that lets them do it online.
findings.fix: Add online booking through the practice’s scheduling system, with a “Book a visit” button in the header of every page and a short request form as a fallback.

findings.title: The phone number is an image
findings.evidence: No phone number appears anywhere in the homepage text (measured: 0 phone numbers found). The number in the header, (305) 555-0187, is part of a graphic; it appears as text only on the contact page.
findings.impact: On a phone it can’t be tapped to call. Screen readers can’t read it, and search engines can’t match it to the practice’s listings.
findings.fix: Set the number as real text with a tap-to-call link in the header and footer of every page, and include it in the practice’s structured data.

findings.title: Nothing is available in Spanish
findings.evidence: No Spanish pages and no hreflang tags (measured). The only Spanish on the homepage is “Se Habla Español” in the footer, while the homepage text says about half of patients prefer Spanish.
findings.impact: Families who search in Spanish are unlikely to find the practice, and those who do land on English-only pages. This works directly against the goal of reaching more Spanish-speaking families.
findings.fix: Publish every page in Spanish under /es/, written or edited by a fluent writer, linked with hreflang tags and an English / Español switch in the header.

findings.title: The homepage is slow on phones
findings.evidence: Google Lighthouse (mobile): performance 34/100, Largest Contentful Paint 6.8 s, First Contentful Paint 3.1 s, Speed Index 7.4 s, Total Blocking Time 1,240 ms. The server took 1.9 s to respond, and the page loads 24 scripts and 14 stylesheets (measured).
findings.impact: Visitors on phones wait several seconds before they see anything useful, and some will leave before the page finishes loading.
findings.fix: Rebuild on a lean, static front end: no slider, compressed and properly sized images, few scripts. Aim for Google’s “good” thresholds: LCP under 2.5 s and layout shift under 0.1.

findings.title: The page is titled “Home”, with no description or H1
findings.evidence: Title tag: “Home” (4 characters). Meta description: empty. H1: none (measured).
findings.impact: In search results Google has to guess what the page is about. “Home” says nothing about dentistry, Coconut Grove or Spanish, the words patients actually search for.
findings.fix: Use a title such as “Family & Cosmetic Dentist in Coconut Grove, Miami | Seagrape Family Dental”, a description that mentions Spanish, same-day emergencies and Saturdays, and one H1 that says what and where the practice is.

findings.title: A stock-photo slider leads the page
findings.evidence: The hero is an auto-rotating slider. Its image files are named like stock photos (“shutterstock_…”), and the captions read “Your Smile Is Our Priority” and “Gentle Care For The Whole Family”. The theme dates from 2016, matching the “© 2016” footer.
findings.impact: Generic photos and rotating slides look like any other practice, push the real strengths below the fold and add weight that slows the page.
findings.fix: Replace the slider with one clear headline, a line about Spanish and same-day care, and Book and Call buttons. Add real photos of the doctors, team and office after a photo shoot.

findings.title: No local business markup or link previews
findings.evidence: No structured data of any kind (measured: no JSON-LD types) and no Open Graph or Twitter card tags (measured).
findings.impact: Google gets no machine-readable confirmation of the practice’s name, address, phone, hours or languages. Links shared on WhatsApp or Facebook show no preview image or description.
findings.fix: Add Dentist (LocalBusiness) schema with address, phone, opening hours, services and languages (English, Spanish), plus Open Graph tags on every page.

findings.title: Services are listed, not explained
findings.evidence: The homepage lists six services as one-line links. The sitemap has 9 URLs (measured), and none is a page for a single service such as Invisalign, implants or emergencies.
findings.impact: People search for specific treatments, like “Invisalign Coconut Grove” or “emergency dentist Miami”. Without a page for each, the site has little to rank for them and little to reassure someone comparing options.
findings.fix: Write one page per core service, in English and Spanish, covering what it is, who it’s for, what a visit is like and how to book.

findings.title: Small, low-contrast text and missing alt text
findings.evidence: 22 of 31 homepage images have no alt text (measured). Lighthouse accessibility is 71/100. The theme stylesheet sets body text at 13px and captions in #999999 on white, about 2.8:1 contrast.
findings.impact: Patients with low vision, and anyone reading a phone in Miami sunlight, will struggle. WCAG AA asks for at least 4.5:1 contrast for body text.
findings.fix: Use 18px body text, colors that meet 4.5:1, descriptive alt text for every meaningful image, and test the new site against WCAG 2.2 AA before launch.

findings.title: The site runs on very old software
findings.evidence: The page’s generator tag reports WordPress 4.5.3 (measured), a version released in 2016.
findings.impact: Out-of-date WordPress installs and plugins are a common target for attacks. A hacked or flagged site would be hard on a healthcare practice’s reputation.
findings.fix: Move to a maintained setup, or a static build with no plugins to patch, with automatic updates, backups and uptime monitoring.

findings.title: Dated news makes the practice look inactive
findings.evidence: The homepage’s “Latest News” block shows posts from December 2017 and March 2016, and the footer reads “© 2016”.
findings.impact: Old dates suggest nobody is minding the site, even though the practice is open six days a week.
findings.fix: Remove the news block and the dated copyright. If the team wants to publish, start with a few useful bilingual guides (see content ideas).

concepts.name: Sea Glass
concepts.tagline: Calm, clear and built around booking.
concepts.idea: This direction keeps things familiar and makes them work: a bright, uncluttered practice site in sea-glass teal where the first screen says what Seagrape is, that the whole team speaks Spanish, and how to book. It suits families who want reassurance and speed more than spectacle, and it is the quickest route to more online bookings.
concepts.bestFor: Busy parents and first-time patients who want to trust the practice at a glance and book in a few taps.

palette.role: Primary buttons, links and the logo

palette.name: Sea Glass
palette.role: Soft panels, cards and the booking card backdrop

palette.name: Coral Signal
palette.role: Emergency band and urgent actions only

typography.rationale: Figtree is a clean, friendly geometric sans that stays warm at headline sizes. Atkinson Hyperlegible Next was designed with the Braille Institute for readers with low vision: a good fit for a practice that sees children and grandparents, and a direct fix for today’s small text.

concepts.heroHeadline: Family dentistry in Coconut Grove, in English or Spanish.
concepts.heroSubhead: Two dentists, cleanings to implants, same-day emergency visits and appointments Monday to Saturday. Book online, or call (305) 555-0187.

sections.name: Hero with booking card
sections.purpose: Headline, subhead, Book and Call buttons, and a booking card that asks for the type of visit and the preferred language.

sections.name: Four reasons
sections.purpose: A strip of plain facts: Hablamos español, same-day emergencies, open Monday to Saturday, two dentists for every age.

sections.name: Services
sections.purpose: Six cards for cleanings and checkups, kids’ visits, Invisalign, whitening, implants and emergencies, each linking to its page.

sections.name: Meet the doctors
sections.purpose: Dr. Elena Ruiz and Dr. Andrés Molina, with the languages they speak and a link to their page.

sections.name: Your first visit
sections.purpose: What happens from booking to the chair, including forms to fill in ahead of time.

sections.name: Emergency band
sections.purpose: A coral band: something hurts today? Call (305) 555-0187 for a same-day visit.

sections.name: Contact and hours
sections.purpose: Coconut Grove location, Monday to Saturday hours, phone, email and an English / Español switch.

concepts.signatureDetail: A booking card on the first screen that asks two questions before anything else, what kind of visit and which language, so a Spanish-speaking parent books a Spanish-speaking visit from the very first tap.
concepts.motion: Quick and quiet: booking options highlight on hover, sections rise a few pixels as they enter, nothing lasts longer than 200 ms, and all of it switches off for people who prefer reduced motion.
pros: Fastest to build and the easiest for the front desk to keep up to date
Booking and the phone number sit on the first screen of every page
Feels trustworthy and clinical in the good sense
tradeoffs: Less memorable than the other two directions; it wins on clarity, not personality

concepts.name: Under the Seagrape
concepts.tagline: Warm, sunlit care for every generation.
concepts.idea: Sea grape trees shade Miami’s shoreline, and families gather under them. This direction turns the practice’s name into its whole visual world: big round sea grape leaves with their red veins, warm morning light and soft color, drawn as illustrations until real photos of the team exist. It leads with how a visit should feel, friendly for kids and reassuring for nervous adults, in both languages.
concepts.bestFor: Parents choosing a dentist for the whole family, and adults who feel anxious about the dentist.

palette.name: Vein Red
palette.role: Leaf veins, small accents and the emergency button

palette.name: Sun Gold
palette.role: The sun, highlights and illustration details (never text)

typography.rationale: Fraunces has soft, rounded serifs that feel warm and personal at large sizes, with none of the chill of a clinical sans. Nunito Sans is friendly and very readable for body text, with full support for Spanish accents.

concepts.heroHeadline: A dentist the whole family can grow up with.
concepts.heroSubhead: Seagrape Family Dental is a bilingual family and cosmetic practice in Coconut Grove: two dentists, a team that speaks English and Spanish, Saturday appointments and same-day care when something hurts.

sections.name: Sunlit hero
sections.purpose: The headline in warm morning light, framed by drawn sea grape leaves, with Book and Call buttons.

sections.name: Hablamos español
sections.purpose: A green band that welcomes Spanish-speaking families in both languages.

sections.name: Care for every age
sections.purpose: Three illustrated cards: kids’ visits, everyday care for adults (cleanings, checkups, implants) and smile makeovers (Invisalign, whitening).

sections.name: Meet your dentists
sections.purpose: Dr. Elena Ruiz and Dr. Andrés Molina, shown in leaf-framed medallions until team photos are ready.

sections.name: A calm first visit
sections.purpose: Three gentle steps from hello to a plan, for kids and for nervous adults.

sections.name: When it can’t wait
sections.purpose: Same-day emergency visits, with a tap-to-call button for (305) 555-0187.

sections.name: Visit us
sections.purpose: An illustrated map of the Grove, hours Monday to Saturday, phone and email.

concepts.signatureDetail: Hand-drawn sea grape leaves, each with the plant’s red veins, frame the hero and return at section edges, so the name becomes a look no other practice can copy.
concepts.motion: Slow and soft: leaves drift a few pixels as you scroll and the morning light warms as the page loads. Buttons lift gently. All motion stops for reduced-motion settings.
pros: The most emotionally appealing to parents and anxious patients
Turns the practice’s name into a memorable, ownable look
Illustrations look finished now and pair well with real photos later
tradeoffs: Needs real team photos within a few months to feel complete

concepts.name: Hola, Grove
concepts.idea: Seagrape’s clearest advantage is language: its own site says about half of patients prefer Spanish, and the whole team speaks it. This direction makes that the design. Every headline is set in English and Spanish side by side, in big confident type on a deep sea grape green, like the cover of a bilingual Miami magazine.
concepts.bestFor: Spanish-speaking families, and younger adults looking for Invisalign or whitening from a practice that feels local, not corporate.

palette.name: Grape Coral
palette.role: Spanish text and the same-day block

typography.rationale: Bricolage Grotesque has the punch and character to carry very large headlines in two languages, and its narrow widths let English and Spanish sit side by side. Newsreader is a screen serif made for reading, which gives the copy an editorial, magazine feel.

concepts.heroHeadline: Your dentist, in your language. Tu dentista, en tu idioma.
concepts.heroSubhead: Family and cosmetic dentistry in Coconut Grove, with a team that speaks English and Spanish. Odontología familiar y estética en Coconut Grove, con un equipo que habla inglés y español.

sections.name: One team, two languages
sections.purpose: A short statement, in both languages, that everyone on the team speaks English and Spanish.

sections.name: Service index
sections.purpose: A large typographic list of services in English and Spanish, each linking to its page.

sections.name: Same-day block
sections.purpose: A coral block: Hurts today? / ¿Te duele hoy? Call (305) 555-0187 for a same-day visit.

sections.name: The doctors

sections.name: The week

sections.name: Sign-off footer

concepts.signatureDetail: Every headline is set twice, English in white and Spanish in coral, side by side, so a Spanish-speaking family sees itself on the first screen without hunting for a language switch.
concepts.motion: Typographic: headlines slide in line by line, the Spanish line arriving a beat after the English, and service names underline as you hover. Short, and off for reduced-motion settings.
pros: Speaks straight to Spanish-speaking families, the practice’s stated growth goal

Every line must be written well in two languages, which adds editing time
